content.title: When is March Madness? 2026 NCAA Tournament dates, TV schedule, locations, odds
content.text: March 15, 2026Updated March 16, 2026, 12:50 a.m. ETMarch Madness is finally here.The one-of-a-kind postseason tournament that captivates the hearts of die-hard and first-time college basketball fans alike kicks off at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, March 15 when the 68-team bracket is revealed one seed line after another on CBS.The actual Road to Indianapolis begins on Tuesday in Dayton with the First Four play-in tournament, while first-round games begin at a variety of different arenas around the country.How will March Madness play out this year? Will there be a Final Four of all No. 1 seeds again? Will Cameron Boozer help push Duke over the line and snap the Blue Devils' national championship drought? Will there be a Cinderella team this year? Will the Big Ten's championship drought end?All of those questions, among others, will play out and be answered over the next few weeks.Here's what you need to know for the 2026 NCAA Tournament from TV schedule, results, streaming options, game site information, national championship betting odds and much more: March Madness Bracket 2026The full 68-team March Madness bracket was revealed at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, March 15 during the NCAA Tournament Selection Sunday Show on CBS. Full 2026 NCAA Tournament scheduleStart date: Tuesday, March 17 (First Four)End date: Monday, April 6 (national championship)March Madness gets officially underway with the First Four on Tuesday, March 17 at UD Arena in Dayton, Ohio. First-round games will officially kick off on Thursday, March 19.Here’s a full breakdown of the schedule for the 2026 NCAA men's tournament:First Four: March 17-18First round: March 19-20Second round: March 21-22Sweet 16: March 26-27Elite Eight: March 28-29Final Four: Saturday, April 4 (at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis)National championship game: Monday, April 6 (at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis)Stream select March Madness games with SlingTVWhen is the First Four?The First Four of the men's NCAA Tournament tips off on Tuesday, March 17 at 6:40 p.m. ET. It will carry into Wednesday, March 18, and consist of four total games, with two games taking place on each day.Here's a breakdown of the First Four schedule for the 2026 NCAA Tournament:Tuesday, March 17Game 1: No. 11 NC State vs. No. 11 Texas | TBDGamer 2: No. 16 UMBC vs. No. 16 UMBC | TBDTV channel: truTVStreaming options: March Madness Live app and SlingTVWednesday, March 18Game 1: No. 11 Miami (OH) vs. SMU | TBDGamer 2: No. 16 Prairie View A&M vs. Lehigh | TBDTV channel: truTVStreaming options: March Madness Live app and SlingTVWhen is the Final Four?The Final Four returns to Indianapolis and Lucas Oil Stadium this year on Saturday, April 4. It is the first time the Final Four has returned to Indianapolis since the "COVID-19 Pandemic Bubble" NCAA Tournament in 2021.Here's a breakdown of dates and tip-off times for the Final Four and the national championship game:Final FourDate: Saturday, April 4Time: Game 1: 6 p.m. ET | Game 2: 8:30 p.m. ETTV channel: TBSStreaming options: March Madness Live app and SlingTVMarch Madness National ChampionshipDate: Monday, April 6Time: 8:30 p.m. ETTV channel: TBSStreaming options: March Madness Live app and SlingTVStream select March Madness games with Fubo (free trial)How to watch March Madness 2026 games? TV channels, streaming optionsTV channels: CBS | TBS | TNT | truTVStreaming options: March Madness Live app | SlingTV | Fubo (free trial) | Paramount+Like past years, the NCAA Tournament will be carried across an assortment of different networks owned by CBS and Warner Bros. Discovery, including CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV.To stream the games that will appear on Warner Bros. Discovery, the parent company of Turner Sports, networks — TBS, TNT and truTV — one streaming option includes Sling TV. To stream the games that will appear on CBS, two streaming options are Fubo, which carries CBS and offers a free trial to new subscribers, and Paramount+, CBS's subscription streaming service.Additionally, all March Madness games can be streamed on the March Madness Live app (with a TV login).Here are the regional weekend announcer crews:Ian Eagle, Bill Raftery, Grant Hill and Tracy WolfsonBrian Anderson, Jim Jackson and Allie LaForceKevin Harlan, Robbie Hummel, Stan Van Gundy and and Lauren ShehadiAndrew Catalon, Steve Lappas and Evan WashburnHere are the other March Madness broadcast crews, in alphabetical order:Spero Dedes, Jim Spanarkel and Jon RothsteinBrandon Gaudin, Chris Webber and Andy KatzTom McCarthy, Candace Parker, Dan Bonner and AJ RossBrad Nessler, Wally Szczerbiak and Jared GreenbergMarch Madness 2026 locationsHere is a full breakdown of which sites and locations will host the NCAA Tournament this season:First Four:UD Arena (Dayton, Ohio)Rounds 1-2:KeyBank Center (Buffalo, New York)Bon Secours Wellness Arena (Greenville, South Carolina)Paycom Center (Oklahoma City)Moda Center (Portland, Oregon)Benchmark International Arena (Tampa)Xfinity Mobile Arena (Philadelphia)Viejas Arena (San Diego)Enterprise Arena (St. Louis)Sweet 16-Elite 8:East Regional: Capital One Arena (Washington, D.C.)South Regional: Toyota Center (Houston)Midwest Regional: United Center (Chicago)West Regional: SAP Center (San Jose, California)Final Four-National Championship:Lucas Oil Stadium (Indianapolis)March Madness 2026 oddsHere's a full list of the best odds for teams to win the national championship (as of Saturday, March 14), per BetMGM:1.
